QuestionStmt.S: The solubility of salt BA$_2$ is $4 \times 10^{-4}$ mol dm$^{-3}$. What is solubility product of the salt?

Solution.S:
Let the salt be BA$_2$. It dissociates as:

$$\mathrm{BA_2(s) \rightleftharpoons B^{2+}(aq) + 2A^-(aq)}$$

Let solubility be $s = 4 \times 10^{-4}$ mol dm$^{-3}$.

At equilibrium: $[B^{2+}] = s = 4 \times 10^{-4}$ and $[A^-] = 2s = 8 \times 10^{-4}$.

Solubility product: $K_{sp} = [B^{2+}][A^-]^2 = (4 \times 10^{-4}) \times (8 \times 10^{-4})^2$.

$$= (4 \times 10^{-4}) \times (64 \times 10^{-8}) = 256 \times 10^{-12} = 2.56 \times 10^{-10}$$

Thus the correct option is B: $2.56 \times 10^{-10}$.
